entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Alfonso Petrucci, a scion of Siena's most powerful family, rose to prominence as an Italian cardinal, though his career was tragically cut short by his involvement in a conspiracy against Pope Leo X. Born to Pandolfo Petrucci, the de facto ruler of Siena, Alfonso inherited a legacy of shrewd political maneuvering and a desire to secure his family's influence not only in Tuscany but within the highest echelons of the Roman Catholic Church. His elevation to cardinal in 1511, at the young age of 24, was a testament to his family's considerable diplomatic and financial leverage, designed to cement the Petrucci dynasty's power and provide a vital ecclesiastical link in an era of intense Italian political fragmentation and papal ambition.

The core of Petrucci's historical significance lies in his central role in the so-called "Conspiracy of the Cardinals" of 1517. Disgruntled by Pope Leo X's perceived tyranny, financial demands, and perceived anti-Sienese policies, Cardinal Petrucci allegedly spearheaded a plot, alongside other cardinals like Adriano Castellesi and Bandinello Sauli, to poison the pontiff. The conspiracy was uncovered, reportedly through intercepted letters and the confession of a co-conspirator. Petrucci was lured back to Rome under false assurances of safety, arrested, imprisoned in Castel Sant'Angelo, and subjected to torture. Despite his initial denial, he eventually confessed under duress, admitting to the plot.
